title: Integrable metrics and effectivity with controlled boundary
main_claim: Thm 1.1: Y is smooth projective and C>=0 is an integral divisor. If -K_Y+C has a singular metric with a global strict curvature lower bound and J(h) ⊃ O(-C), then every pseudoeffective rational M has an effective rational C_0 supported on C with M+C_0 rationally effective. Thm conv:fixed-error: X is smooth projective, -K_X=L has a smooth semipositive metric and P is pseudoeffective Cartier. If effective N_j ~ m_jL-P exist for unbounded m_j, then H^0(X,mL)≠0 for some m>0. Corollary: the same conclusion follows from twisted (Ω^1)^{⊗p} or Ω^p sections.

issues.description: The pseudoeffectivity of -det of the saturated cotangent-tensor subsheaf is taken from LMPTX Thm 4.1 (Ou's generic nefness) as a black box. Its hypothesis, -K_X nef, holds here. The paper also gives a second, movable-slope proof of this step, which I did not fully verify.
issues.evidence: 'The cotangent-subsheaf consequence of generic tangent nefness [LMPTX, Thm 4.1] gives -A pseudoeffective.'

issues.description: The alternative toroidal metric route depends on CompanionG Thm 2.1, and the invariant/isometric applications depend on CompanionI Thm 1.1 and CompanionH Thm 2.1/Lemma 2.2, all used as black boxes. The headline theorems (Thm 1.1 and conv:fixed-error) do not depend on them.
issues.evidence: 'These are the hypotheses of the toroidal-volume theorem in [CompanionG, Theorem 2.1]'

coverage: I checked these in detail: Lemma 2.1, the weighted approximation argument (Nadel + Castelnuovo–Mumford global generation giving b_r ⊃ J(rφ), the OT point-extension bound φ∘σ ≤ (a/r)log|t|^2 + O(1), and the integrability bound a/r - j - k < 1); Thm 2.2, the signed adjoint identity (algebra re-derived); and the proof of Thm 1.1 (klt and big for Δ_t, the hypotheses of BCHM Thm D, rational recovery, and pushforward support). In the conversion theorem I checked: the affine identity for N_j (degree bookkeeping), nonnegativity of the horizontal part, pseudoeffectivity of M via J/(m_j-m_0), the flattening model condition, the rank-one argument through Iitaka maximality, that f^*C is exceptional, the mixed metric with J(h)=O_Z, the application of PT18 Thm 3.3.5 together with the strict-bound twist, finite norm of s_C, and the return lemma. I also checked: the all-dominated alternative (the degrees of u_j^r u_1^{m_j-m_2}, the fiber-integral exponent (a+1-e)/e ≤ floor(a/e), and admissibility in the rank-one argument); the integrable-neighborhood lemma (Hölder mixing); Lemma conv:null-curvature; the determinant-extraction slot argument; and Lemma inv:null-slope (Hermite–Einstein/Bochner). The smooth-coarea, jet-bigness, fano-auxiliary and extremal-tensor sections, and most of the invariant section, were only skimmed.
sibling_notes: The sibling papers in family 068 (rank 6, 22, 89, 218) were all no_gap_found and treated LMPTX Thm 4.1 and CompanionG/H/I as black boxes in the same way. This paper's Thm 1.1 and conversion proof are self-contained apart from standard citations: Nadel, OT/Demailly, BCHM Thm D, PT18, Boucksom, Guan–Zhou, Skoda.
